source.title: Why is AI generated language so hard to understand?
source.author: canjobear

title.zh: AI生成语言为何难以理解
title.en: Why AI-Generated Language Is Hard to Understand

excerpt.zh: AI生成语言研究发现，大型模型更常使用低频词组、复杂依存结构和高信息密度表达，这可能牺牲了人类读者的处理效率。
excerpt.en: Research on AI-generated language finds that large models use more rare phrases, complex dependencies, and dense wording, potentially making text harder for people to process.

text.en: Why AI-Generated Language Feels Harder to Read

text.zh: 一篇发表于arXiv的研究考察了人们普遍感受到的现象：AI生成语言往往比人类写作更难理解。研究团队分析了跨领域的AI文本，并将其与人工写作及机器翻译往返改写的文本进行比较，重点关注会增加人类处理负担的语言特征。
text.en: An arXiv study examines a common impression: AI-generated language can be harder to understand than human writing. The researchers analyzed AI text across domains and compared it with human writing and round-trip translation paraphrases, focusing on linguistic features known to increase processing demands.

text.zh: 研究摘要称，九个前沿及接近前沿的模型都更常使用无生命主语搭配有生命动词，以及低频词组；多数模型还表现出更长的句法依存、更密集的名词堆叠，以及对话中更多省略关系从句。作者提出，这可能与模型被优化来处理数学、代码和推理任务有关：这些任务鼓励在较短篇幅中承载更多信息，而人类语言通常更强调顺畅、成功的沟通。不同模型家族之间仍存在明显差异。
text.en: The abstract reports that all nine frontier and near-frontier models used more inanimate subjects with animate verbs and more low-frequency n-grams. Most also showed longer syntactic dependencies, denser noun stacking, and more reduced object relatives in conversation. The authors suggest that this may reflect optimization for mathematics, code, and reasoning, where compact information density is valuable, while human language is more strongly shaped by successful communication. The study also found substantial variation across model families.

text.zh: 可读性问题仍需进一步验证
作者用一个概念验证支持这一假设：对模型施加长度惩罚后，其语言行为进一步偏离人类写作。这个结果提示，提升AI文本可读性不能只依靠缩短篇幅，还可能需要直接优化人类读者的处理负担。不过，现有摘要没有说明不同读者群体、任务类型或编辑提示会如何改变结果，也没有证明所有AI文本都必然难懂。后续研究需要更广泛的语料和真实阅读测试，才能确定哪些语言特征最值得优先修正。
text.en: A proof-of-concept supported the hypothesis: applying a length penalty caused a model's linguistic behavior to diverge further from human writing. This suggests that improving AI readability may require optimizing for readers' processing demands, not simply shortening output. However, the abstract does not establish how audience, task, or editing prompts change the effect, nor does it show that all AI text is necessarily difficult. Broader corpora and real reading tests are needed to identify which features deserve priority.
